title: 1972 AHSME Problem 32
statement: Chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) in the circle shown intersect at \(E\) and are perpendicular to each other. If segments \(AE,\) \(EB,\) and \(ED\) have measures \(2,\) \(6,\) and \(3\) respectively, then the length of the diameter of the circle is:

solutions.text:
The intersecting-chords theorem gives \[ 2\cdot6=CE\cdot3, \] so \(CE=4.\) Put \(E=(0,0),\) \(A=(-2,0),\) \(B=(6,0),\) \(C=(0,4),\) and \(D=(0,-3).\) The perpendicular bisectors of \(AB\) and \(CD\) meet at \[ O=\left(2,\frac12\right). \] Thus \[ r^2=OA^2=4^2+\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac{65}{4}, \] and the diameter is \(2r=\sqrt{65}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Place \(E\) at the origin; the center is at the intersection of the two chord perpendicular bisectors
